2217.unvetted: Leaf c. 13r seen in Chrome on the BNCF teca viewer (idr BNCF0003827870, thumbnail grid): a strip with four lines of symbol cipher (digits, letters, Greek-like signs, about 75 per line, roughly 300 in all), no gloss. But the strip just before it, c. 12r (same narrow format, stamped 3423195), is a clear Italian note: "El conte Girolamo ha sollecitato l'andata di m. Ascanio a Roma, qual si stima sia opera dello S.re ... el Palavisino ... m. Johanfrancesco ... Strasoldano è sospecto assai parendo loro che lui sia ghibellino", about 300 letters. Two quick checks suggest it may be the clear of c. 13r: the cipher's "11" pair falls where the "ll" of "sollecitato" (line 1) and "ghibellino" (end) would be, and a near-repeat ("s q s 3 n m π b t" / "s y s 3 n π b t") fits the two "Palavisino" at matching positions. A full alignment was not done. Edition check: archive.org full-text search of Lorenzo de' Medici, Lettere V, VI and VII (bwb_KU-999-230_5, -229_6, -231) finds GC 137 cited only for cc. 4, 6-9, 20-21, 22-23/26/35, 32-33/47, 38-39, 45-46, 48-51, never c. 13. The Censimento (1964, Google Books seEYGFQqM1kC) has "137, c. 13" on p. 48 together with 1481, giu/lug/ago, Michelozzi, Ridolfi, Milano: a Lorenzo letter of summer 1481, entry text not readable. Next: align c. 13r with c. 12r. If it fits, the verdict is read (contemporary clear); if not, the lead is open.
